PSA to parents of high school boys...
From a mom of high school girls...

You may not be aware, but some of your sons do not know that they should be providing a corsage and boutonniere for their homecoming and/or prom dates. They don't know how to obtain them and they could use some guidance. If you've already educated your sons on this timeless tradition, I applaud you.

My daughter and her friend are both providing their own corsages and boutonnieres because their dates said they don't know how to take care of getting them. 

I'm not complaining about my daughter providing the flowers. That is not the purpose of my post. The purpose of my post is to make other parents aware that maybe their sons don't know they need to do that.

Please do not bombard my post with negative comments, comments about this issue being a non-issue because of gender inequality, or your political views. Your negative comments are welcome to remain in your negative headspace.

At-home service dogs are trained to perform disability-mitigating tasks that can increase a person’s independence, safety, and overall quality of life. 🐕‍🦺❤️

They are not “lesser” service dogs simply because their work happens primarily at home.

In fact, even many service dogs who regularly work in public access perform some of their most important and valued tasks behind closed doors—where no one else ever sees them.

A service dog’s value isn’t determined by how often they go to the grocery store, restaurants, appointments, or other public places. It’s determined by the meaningful assistance they provide to their handler.

Service dog work doesn’t have to happen in public to matter. ❤️🐾
